name: Excimer laser for stretch marks

lead: The excimer laser is a 308 nm ultraviolet device used in dermatology, and it has been tried on stretch marks that have faded to white.
The sources reviewed show one small phase 1 trial registration without listed results, so the effect on stretch marks is not established here.

paras: Proponents say the ultraviolet light stimulates pigment-producing cells in the pale marks so they darken toward the surrounding skin tone.
The sources reviewed give no safety data for this use. Ultraviolet treatments in general carry considerations that clinicians weigh, but none are documented in the sources used for this article.

trials.title: The Efficacy of 308nm Excimer Laser in White Striae

lead: The 308 nm excimer laser is an ultraviolet light device that is used in dermatology for conditions such as vitiligo and psoriasis. It has also been studied for white (mature) stretch marks, striae alba, which are pale because the skin has lost pigment [1].

Stretch marks begin red or purple and later fade to a pale, atrophic appearance [1]. Proponents of excimer treatment say the ultraviolet light stimulates pigment cells to repigment white marks. Wikipedia, citing a 2014 systematic review, states that no stretch-mark treatment has been clearly shown to be effective once marks have formed, and it does not discuss excimer laser specifically [1].
The sources reviewed include one small registered study, a 10-person phase 1 trial of 308 nm excimer laser in white striae, with no results listed in the registry record [2].

paras: Excimer lasers emit 308 nm ultraviolet B light in a narrow beam. In repigmentation treatments, the light is directed at pale areas, and proponents say it encourages melanocytes to produce pigment so the mark blends more closely with surrounding skin. The sources reviewed give no device settings and none are described here.

NCT00361361, titled The Efficacy of 308nm Excimer Laser in White Striae, was a phase 1 study that began in July 2006 with 10 participants and is listed as completed; no outcome data were available in the registry record reviewed [2]. No other studies on this use were examined for this article.

The procedure is mentioned in skin and body-improvement discussions as an option for stretch marks that have already turned white. No forum material was available for this entry, so community claims are not documented in detail.

timeline.event: A phase 1 study of 308 nm excimer laser in white striae begins with 10 participants (NCT00361361). [2]
